speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The philosophy that each of us is responsible and empowered to take charge of our lifelong learning continues to underpin SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, the funding and support for CET Centres remain substantial.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: CET Centres must, therefore, continue to be an integral part of SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We must ensure they remain publicly accessible, deliver courses that are relevant to industries and offer progression pathways.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: With the Government going towards industry transformation projects, how would the current suite of CET Centres meet the aggregated and differentiated demand and needs of workers, especially existing workers in the workforce?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Throughout these 10-12 years of this work, we went through a Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We set up CET Centres and rolled out programmes that were needed by workers at that point in time.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This will have to be a tripartite effort.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the Ministry be open to include non-CET Centres, such as private companies or organisations that provide skills training in areas, such as sports or the arts?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, you can have a company that deals with football but they have certification courses in football refereeing that may provide opportunities for those who are seeking a second career to be referees in that sport, for instance.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think maybe the differentiation the Member wants to make is not so much between companies or non-companies because even CET Centres are companies – they are training providers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But maybe what the Member is referring to are employers or non-employers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We do support employers because some of their workers are vulnerable or they are trying to raise their productivity.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, as part of SkillsFuture, we can support them – to raise the capabilities of their workers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But there are also other employers who are trying to provide training for the entire industry and we have them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In those cases, we have to ask them to set up a separate entity, negotiate the terms so that it continues to be open, accessible to the entire industry.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And the entire industry must also be comfortable – that I am sending my workers to a particular company, maybe my competitor, for training.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think industry players have to start working together to raise the standard of the industry overall.
